story.title: Our Story
story.p1: Potato Apparel was founded in 2014 with a clear mission: to make professional garment manufacturing accessible to independent designers and emerging brands. We saw too many great ideas stall because MOQs were too high, communication was too poor, and quality was too inconsistent.
story.p2: What started as a small sourcing operation in Guangzhou has grown into a full-service manufacturing partner. We work with a carefully vetted network of specialist factories — matching each product to the facility best equipped to make it — while we manage design, sampling, quality control, and logistics end to end. Today we serve brands across 30+ countries, from solo designers launching a first collection to established labels scaling production.
story.p3: What hasn't changed is our commitment: every client, regardless of order size, receives the same dedicated attention and craftsmanship.

meta.title: Free Apparel Cost & Margin Calculator | Potato Apparel
meta.description: Free calculator for clothing brands: enter your unit cost, freight, duty and retail price to instantly see landed cost, gross margin and profit per piece.

tools.intro: Work out the real economics of your clothing order in seconds. Enter your numbers below to see your landed unit cost, gross margin, and profit per piece — so you can price with confidence before you commit to production.
tools.how1: Landed unit cost is your ex-factory price plus import duty (calculated on the ex-factory value), plus freight per unit and any other per-unit fees. This is the true cost to get one finished piece into your warehouse — always price off this number, not the factory price alone.
tools.how2: Gross margin is profit per unit divided by retail price, shown as a percentage. As a rough guide, apparel brands target 50%+ gross margin to leave room for marketing, returns, and platform fees. Markup shows how many times your landed cost the retail price is.
tools.how3: These figures are gross — they do not include marketing spend, payment processing, returns, or overheads. Use them as a starting point for your pricing, then layer in your operating costs.
tools.ctaTitle: Ready to get a real quote?
tools.relatedPrefix: New to import costs? Read our guide:

in.unitCostHint: Price per piece from the manufacturer
in.qtyHint: Number of pieces in this order
in.dutyHint: Duty rate for your country & product
in.retailHint: What you sell one piece for

verdict.good: Healthy margin. 50%+ gross typically leaves room for marketing, returns and fees.
verdict.ok: Workable margin, but tight. Below ~50% gross, marketing and returns eat profit fast — look for ways to lower landed cost or raise price.
verdict.low: Margin is low. After marketing, fees and returns this may not be profitable. Consider a higher retail price, a larger order for a lower unit cost, or a lighter spec.

calc.disclaimer: Estimates only. Gross figures exclude marketing, payment fees, returns and overheads. Duty rates vary by country and product — confirm with your customs authority or broker.

meta.title: Free Tech Pack Template for Clothing (Printable) | Potato Apparel
meta.description: A free, printable garment tech pack template — BOM, measurement spec, colorways, construction, artwork and labels. Fill it in and send it to your manufacturer.

techpack.intro: A clear tech pack is the difference between a sample that comes back right and one that wastes weeks. Use this free template — print it or save as PDF, fill it in, and send it to your manufacturer.
techpack.printHint: Print it, or use "Save as PDF" in the print dialog to keep a digital copy.
techpack.why1: A tech pack is the blueprint of your garment — measurements, materials, construction, colorways, artwork, and labels in one document. It removes guesswork, reduces sample rounds, and protects you if a production run comes back wrong.
techpack.why2: You do not need to fill in every field on day one. Start with the sketch, fabric, and key measurements; a good manufacturer will help you complete the rest during sampling.
